The runner patches the generated-values ConfigMap and later this admission ConfigMap, but never verifies that the running producer has observed the first update before exposing the permit. Mounted ConfigMap updates are only eventually projected and may be delayed by the kubelet sync/cache interval ([Kubernetes documentation](https://v1-35.docs.kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-pod-configmap/)); if the admission update becomes visible first, LoadGen hashes the stale `-pending` generated values and fails, and a slow start-line run can also leave too little of LoadGen's fixed 180-second admission deadline for the permit update to arrive.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate start-line inputs before creating the Kafka session**

When the packaged scenario/profile differs from the generated comparison document, the start-line path creates the native Kafka session and derives the new broker inventory without calling `GeneratedValuesCompatibility.Validate`; only the later verify-mode pod performs that check. Because `DeploymentGenerator` supplies `PARCHWELL_GENERATED_VALUES_FILE` to start-line too, this permits an unverified Kafka configuration to establish the offsets and broker inventory before the mismatch is detected. Register the scenario resolver for start-line and validate the comparison before `sessions.Create`.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L84-L86](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/eventhubs-kafka-dotnet/blob/f79c74cf23f5d0a1d30b399728f265c82208e676/AGENTS.md#L84-L86)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recover cleanup receipts after swept state disappears**

When an aged sweep successfully applies the destroy plan but cleanup-receipt upload or `MarkDestroyedAsync` then fails—for example because the shared cleanup token expires—Terraform state is already empty while the ledger still lacks a complete destroy receipt. Every scheduled retry returns here before reading the unresolved ledger, so `RunLedger.ReserveAsync` permanently blocks later phases; recover the unique unresolved ledger generation when state is empty or make receipt persistence independently retryable after a successful destroy.

+          out=pathlib.Path(os.environ['A01_OUTPUT']); runtime=json.loads((out/'runtime.json').read_text())
+          acr=runtime['persistent_outputs']['acr']; acr=acr.get('value',acr)
+          sha=runtime['source_commit']; registry=acr['login_server']; name=acr['name']
+          assert re.fullmatch('[a-z0-9]+',name) and re.fullmatch('[a-z0-9.-]+',registry)
+          with (out/'image-publication.log').open('wb') as log:

+                  assert re.fullmatch('sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}',digest)

+          (out/'image-receipts.json').write_text(json.dumps(runtime['images']))

+      - name: Run phase with durable reservation and guarded cleanup
+        id: phase
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          timeout 9600 dotnet src/Parchwell.Runner/bin/Release/net10.0/Parchwell.Runner.dll phase --input "$A01_OUTPUT/runtime.json" --output "$A01_OUTPUT/phase" > "$A01_OUTPUT/phase.log" 2>&1

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Give the gate command its declared job budget**

When the probe gate takes close to its permitted 60-second verifier lifetime, this wrapper kills the entire Runner at 60 seconds, before Runner can inspect the output, upload it, record the gate receipt, and refresh the candidate. The committed runtime contract deliberately gives the enclosing gate job 90 seconds; GNU `timeout --help` confirms that `timeout 60` kills the command after 60 seconds, so use the declared 90-second job budget rather than the inner verifier watchdog.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor the full shared admission deadline**

When producer scheduling takes between 120 and 180 seconds, this hard-coded subtraction throws `producer_admission_deadline` even though `RepeatExecutor` has already supplied the single configured 180-second token that also covers comparison, start-line, and release. The runtime contract does not define a separate 60-second reserve, so this can discard a pod whose remaining steps would still finish within the shared deadline; let that token enforce the declared bound or add an explicit sub-budget.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read replay results from the immutable phase export**

If the probe is completely exported and destroyed but the process terminates or gate recording fails before `RecordGateAsync`, the next dispatch treats the phase as already completed without recreating its local repeat directories, so this read fails even though `probe.PrivateExport` contains all five hash-verified results. The gate then cannot be replayed and C0/C3 remain permanently blocked; `PhaseCandidate` has the same local-only fallback when refreshing actual costs, so load replay inputs through `EvidenceExporter.ReadVerifiedFileAsync` from the immutable phase export.
